findings.text: Any `**` that is not one of the three forms the goal lists becomes `.*`, which crosses `/`. So `a/**b` matches `a/x/yb`, and `a**` matches `ab/c`. The goal says `*` never crosses `/`, and in git such `**` behaves like a single `*`. A related case: `a/**/**/b` compiles to `a/(?:.*/)?.*/b`, which does not match `a/b`, although the goal says `a/**/b` should include `a/b`.

If `.locignore` starts with a UTF-8 BOM, the BOM stays at the start of the first pattern. That pattern then silently never matches; if it is a comment, `#` is no longer the first character, so the comment line becomes a pattern.
Only ENOENT counts as "no .locignore". If a folder is named `.locignore`, readFile throws EISDIR, and that error makes scanFolder and the command fail. They should treat it as having no ignore file.

The test 'escapes regex characters' does not check that `.` is escaped. `aa(b)xtxt` fails to match because of the `+` and parentheses, not because of the `.`, and the positive case passes even with an unescaped `.`. If `.` were dropped from `escape`, every assertion would still pass. A negative case like `a+(b)xtxt` would test it.
The `**/x matches x at any depth` test has only positive assertions. A compile of `**/fixtures` to `.*fixtures` would also pass. It needs a negative case such as `xfixtures` or `a/xfixtures`.
Nothing tests the command's `--no-ignore` option, or that the command honours `.locignore`. The goal requires both, and no CLI test exists.

blind.summary: The goal is met: there are no blockers and no major bugs. I checked by reading the code only; I did not run `npm run check`. The `.locignore` syntax rules are handled correctly: comments, trailing spaces, CRLF, anchoring, folder-only patterns, `**/x`, `x/**`, `a/**/b`, `?`, `!` with last-match-wins, and the rule that a file in an ignored folder can't be re-included. scanFolder skips ignored folders without descending into them and still counts `.locignore`, and the command takes `--no-ignore`. What's left is minor: `**` outside the three listed forms crosses `/`; a BOM at the start of `.locignore` breaks its first line; a folder named `.locignore` makes the scan fail; two tests have gaps (the `.` escape is never checked, and `**/x` has no negative case); and the CLI flag has no test.
